title: GPU Burn Lifecycle Scenarios — Regional $/1M Token & Capacity Mapper
sheet_summary: Compact scenario sheet to compare GPU-hour burn and resulting $/1M token unit economics across NA/EU/APAC under four operational strategies (baseline, reserve-heavy, aggressive-spot, latency-priority). Purpose: give product and finance a lightweight decision matrix for reserved commitments vs spot/ondemand burst and expected unit cost sensitivity.
assumptions: tokens_per_gpu_hour is workload-dependent; we use conservative and optimistic estimates per scenario
GPU list price effective rate includes data transfer and infra overhead (network + storage) baked into $/gpu_hour
Reserved commit discounts: NA 40%, EU 38%, APAC 30% applied to base rack rate
Spot availability modeled as 70% mean for NA, 55% EU, 45% APAC in aggressive-spot scenario
KV cache and batching optimizations reduce effective tokens-per-hour variance by up to 25% in optimized scenarios
key_takeaways: 1) Reserve-heavy wins on unit cost in stable high-util markets (NA/EU) but requires capital commit; 2) Aggressive-spot can reduce apparent $/1M tokens but increases availability risk in APAC — not recommended for latency-sensitive SLAs; 3) Optimized caching + batching materially increases tokens/hour and shifts the curve, often outperforming small additional reserved commits; 4) Latency-priority scenarios carry a premium per 1M tokens and should be limited to SLAs that require <p95 150ms inference windows.
recommended_next_steps: Run a 30-day real workload A/B (baseline vs optimized-caching) in NA and EU with telemetry tag to validate est_tokens_per_gpu_hour uplift; produce a finance-ready commit proposal for a staggered reserved purchase in NA to cover 50% of projected baseline steady-state demand; add a simple dashboard tile to Console showing live $/1M token by region and a small playbook for automatic fallback from reserved -> spot when p95 latency under threshold.
